says: When the policy inspector opens, it always lists the policy's registry key. It lists the registry value and the client extension only when the policy defines a non-empty one.
A registry value that a policy writes is shown by its kind: 'Delete value' for a deletion, 'Numeric value: <number>' for a number, and 'Text value: "<text>"' for text.
An entry in a policy's list of values shows its own registry key only when it has one, and always shows its registry value name and the value it sets.
A list of affected values shows its default registry key only when one is set, followed by every value the list affects.

The affected registry settings of a policy or element show only the parts it defines: set when enabled, set list when enabled, set when disabled, set list when disabled. When none is defined, the group reads 'Left implicit' if the policy names a registry value, or 'Left to elements' if not.
The presentation part of the inspector is shown only when the policy has both a presentation and policy elements; otherwise only the registry information appears.

Each presentation element shows its details by its type. Labels are shown for number boxes, text boxes, combo boxes and drop-down lists only when non-empty. Numeric boxes show the default and either the spinner increment or 'No spinner'. Check boxes show 'checked' or 'unchecked' as default. Combo boxes and drop-down lists show 'alphabetical' sorting unless they keep ADMX order, and a drop-down shows its default choice number only when one is set.
A combo box lists its suggestions, headed by their count, only when the presentation defines suggestions.

A presentation element with no ID shows no linked policy element; one with an ID is followed by the policy element with that ID, with its type, client extension and registry key shown only when non-empty.
A policy element shows its registry value name unless it is a list element, which has no single value name.
A number element shows its minimum, maximum and whether it is required, plus 'Stored as text' when stored as text and 'Soft' when it does not overwrite an existing value.
A true/false element shows the registry settings it applies when checked and unchecked.
A text element shows its maximum length and whether it is required, plus 'Stored as expandable string' when so stored and 'Soft' when it does not overwrite an existing value.

A list element states how its value names arise: 'User provides value names', or 'Value prefix' with the prefix when it has one, otherwise 'No prefix (values named for their data)'. It adds 'Stored as expandable strings' when so stored and always says whether existing values are preserved.

A choice element shows whether it is required and its number of choices. Each choice, numbered from 0 in order, shows its display code, its display name resolved from the policy's own definition file, its value, and any additional registry settings only when it has some.
Pressing Ctrl+C in the inspector's tree copies the text of the selected line to the clipboard; with no line selected nothing is copied.
Each section's fragment reads the state from that section's own policy source (machine or user), and includes the policy's comment for that section only when a comment exists for it.
A section's fragment lists the option values only when the policy is Enabled in that section; for other states no options are written.
The fragment text begins with the line 'Policy Plus Semantic Policy' followed by a blank line only while the header box is ticked; otherwise only the fragment is shown.
A language code is accepted only when it has exactly two parts separated by a hyphen, such as en-US; otherwise the person is told 'Please enter a valid language code.' and the dialog stays open.
When the entered language equals the current one, the dialog is cancelled and no new language is set; otherwise the entry (trimmed of spaces) becomes the new language and the dialog is accepted.
When names are required in a list, confirming is refused if two entries share a name; the person is told 'Multiple entries are named "<name>"! Remove or rename all but one.' and keeps editing.
Confirming a list without names keeps every row in order as a plain list, ignoring the unfinished blank row; confirming a list with names keeps each name with its value.
A list editor opened with names shows a name column and the existing name and value pairs; opened without names it hides that column and shows the values only.
The all-products list shows top-level products sorted by display name with their count of versions.
Selecting a top-level product lists its major versions sorted by version number with their count of minor versions; with none selected the list is empty and the label asks to select a product.
Selecting a major version lists its minor versions sorted by version number; with none selected the list is empty and the label asks to select a major version.
The support definitions list is sorted by display name ignoring leading spaces, and shows only definitions whose name contains the filter text, ignoring case.
The filter text is cleared each time the support definitions dialog opens, so every definition is listed at first.
Pressing Enter on a loaded definition file or support definition opens its details only when a row is selected.
Pressing Enter on a support definition opens its details only when a row is selected.
The semantic policy fragment includes a section only when the policy applies to that section; a policy for both machine and user shows a machine block then a user block.
Double-clicking a product in any of the three product lists opens its details only when a product is selected.

The affected registry settings of a policy or element show only the parts it defines: set when enabled, set list when enabled, set when disabled, set list when disabled. When none is defined, the group reads 'Left implicit' if the policy names a registry value, or 'Left to elements' if not. For a true/false element nothing is ever treated as a registry value, so an element defining none always reads 'Left implicit'.
A number box in the presentation shows its label only when non-empty, always its default, and either 'Spinner increment: <n>' or 'No spinner'.
A presentation label shows its text, even when empty.
A text box in the presentation shows its label only when non-empty, and always its default text, even when empty.
A check box in the presentation always shows its text and its default as 'checked' or 'unchecked'.
A combo box in the presentation shows its label only when non-empty, always its default text, and sorting as 'alphabetical' unless it keeps ADMX order.
A drop-down list in the presentation shows its label only when non-empty, its default choice as '#<number>' only when one is set, and sorting as 'alphabetical' unless it keeps ADMX order.
A list box or multi-line text box in the presentation always shows its label, even when empty.

A presentation element with no ID shows no linked policy element. One with an ID is followed by the policy element with that ID, always showing its type, and its client extension and registry key only when non-empty. The inspector assumes every presentation ID has a matching policy element; when none does, the lookup fails.
Pressing Enter in the loaded definition files list opens the selected file's details only when a row is selected. Double-clicking has no such check, so double-clicking empty space fails.
Pressing Enter in the support definitions list opens the selected definition's details only when a row is selected. Double-clicking has no such check, so double-clicking empty space fails.
Double-clicking, or pressing Enter, on any of the three product lists opens the selected product's details, and does nothing when no product is selected.

Confirming a list without names keeps the value of every row in order as a plain list, ignoring the unfinished blank row; a row takes only its value cell, never a name. Confirming a list with names keeps each name with its value.
In a list with names, a row whose name cell is blank is not checked or refused: its missing name is used as a key, so confirming fails with an error instead of being refused or accepted.
Pressing Enter in the loaded definition files list opens the selected file's details only when a row is selected. Double-clicking has no such check, so double-clicking empty space fails.
Pressing Enter in the support definitions list opens the selected definition's details only when a row is selected. Double-clicking has no such check, so double-clicking empty space fails.
Double-clicking, or pressing Enter, on any of the three product lists opens the selected product's details, and does nothing when no product is selected.
